questions.q: What does setting a report item's Bookmark property actually do?
options: It marks that location as a named jump-to target other items can link to
It hides the item until a user clicks a toggle
It opens a separate drillthrough report
It adds the item's data to the report's document outline automatically
questions.explain: A bookmark is just a label on a location in the report. On its own it does nothing visible — it becomes useful once something else links to it with Go to bookmark.

questions.q: What happens if a bookmark string isn't unique within the report?
options: A link to that bookmark jumps to the first matching bookmark it finds, with no error
SSRS refuses to publish the report
The report automatically renames the duplicate bookmarks
The bookmark link throws a run-time exception
questions.explain: The bookmark string must be unique, but SSRS doesn't enforce that at design time — a duplicate bookmark silently resolves to whichever matching bookmark comes first.

questions.q: Which property adds a report item (or a group's unique values) as an entry in the document map?
options: DocumentMapLabel
Bookmark
ToggleItem
Hidden
questions.explain: DocumentMapLabel, set on the item or on a group's Advanced page as the Document map expression, is what populates the automatic table-of-contents side pane.

questions.q: How does the PDF rendering extension represent a report's document map?
options: As the Bookmarks pane in Acrobat
It ignores document maps entirely, the same as XML or CSV
As a separate PDF file linked from the main report
As a floating overlay window on top of the report
questions.explain: PDF has no live side pane like the HTML viewer, so it translates the document map into Acrobat's Bookmarks pane instead. Excel uses a named worksheet, and Word uses its table of contents.

questions.q: On the Action tab of an item's Properties dialog, which option links that item to a bookmark elsewhere in the same report?
options: Go to bookmark
Go to report
Go to URL
Go to parameter
questions.explain: Go to bookmark targets a bookmark ID (or an expression that evaluates to one) inside the current report — Go to report is the drillthrough option from Lesson 27, and Go to URL targets an external address.
